record.paper_title: Nine open problems on conjunctive and Boolean grammars
record.original_question: Do conjunctive grammars over a one-letter alphabet generate only regular languages, or can a conjunctive grammar generate a nonregular unary language? A conjunctive grammar is a context-free grammar extended with explicit conjunction in rule bodies, without the explicit negation operation available in Boolean grammars.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A conjunctive grammar is a quadruple $G=(\Sigma,N,R,S)$, where $\Sigma$ is a finite alphabet, $N$ is a finite set of nonterminal symbols, $S\in N$ is the start symbol, and $R$ is a finite set of rules of the form
$$A \to \alpha_1 \,\&\, \alpha_2 \,\&\, \cdots \,\&\, \alpha_n,$$
with $A\in N$, $n\ge 1$, and each $\alpha_i\in(\Sigma\cup N)^*$. The language generated by such a rule consists of all strings $w\in\Sigma^*$ that can be derived from each of the conjuncts $\alpha_i$; formally, the languages $L_G(A)\subseteq\Sigma^*$ for $A\in N$ are defined as the least solution of the system of equations
$$L_G(A) \;=\; \bigcup_{A\to\alpha_1\&\cdots\&\alpha_n\in R}\; \bigcap_{i=1}^{n} \widehat{\alpha_i}, \qquad A\in N,$$
where $\widehat{\alpha}$ denotes the language obtained from $\alpha$ by concatenation, with each nonterminal $B$ replaced by $L_G(B)$. The language generated by $G$ is $L(G)=L_G(S)$. Negation is not permitted.

Question: Does there exist a conjunctive grammar $G$ over a one-letter alphabet $\Sigma=\{a\}$ such that $L(G)\subseteq\{a\}^*$ is not a regular language? Equivalently, are all unary languages generated by conjunctive grammars regular?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was solved by Artur Jeż, who constructed a conjunctive grammar generating the non-regular unary language $\{a^{4^n}: n\ge 0\}$, first announced in 2007 (DLT) and published in International Journal of Foundations of Computer Science (2008). Subsequent work generalized this to broader classes of unary languages generated by conjunctive grammars.

status_evidence.title: Conjunctive Grammars Can Generate Non-regular Unary Languages
status_evidence.snippet: Jeż constructs a conjunctive grammar for {a^{4^n} : n ≥ 0}, a non-regular unary language.
status_evidence.claim: A conjunctive grammar generating a non-regular unary language exists; hence the problem is solved in the negative.

status_evidence.title: CONJUNCTIVE GRAMMARS GENERATE NON-REGULAR UNARY LANGUAGES
status_evidence.snippet: Journal version (IJFCS 2008) establishing that conjunctive grammars over a unary alphabet can generate non-regular languages.
status_evidence.claim: The unary regularity question for conjunctive grammars is resolved: non-regular unary languages can be generated.

status_evidence.title: Conjunctive Grammars over a Unary Alphabet: Undecidability and Unbounded Growth
status_evidence.snippet: Follow-up work extending the class of unary languages generated by conjunctive grammars and establishing undecidability properties.
status_evidence.claim: Further results confirm and extend the resolution of the unary conjunctive-grammar problem.
